content.title: Incredible comeback sends Hawks to shocking Game 2 win vs. Knicks
content.text: Director Spike Lee attends Game 2 of the Eastern Conference first round NBA playoffs at Madison Square Garden on April 20, 2026 in New York City.Al Bello/Getty Images Knicks vs. Hawks: Atlanta pulls off remarkable Game 2 comeback, wins 107-106 Frantic final scene at MSG CJ McCollum, who scored a game-high 32 points, missed a pair of free throws with 5.6 seconds left. The Knicks got the rebound, but Mikal Bridges missed the potential game-winning shot at Monday’s buzzer at Madison Square Garden.Article continues below this adBefore McCollum missed those free throws, the Hawks had outscored the Knicks 28-15 in the fourth quarter. New York had led 100-92 midway through the final period, but the Hawks used an 11-0 run to seize momentum.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.ONLY 25¢The win for the Hawks evened the playoff series at 1-1. Knicks stats to know Jalen Brunson scored 29 points, but was 10 of 26 from the field. Karl-Anthony Towns scored 18 points, but none in the fourth quarter. Josh Hart had a double-double with 15 points and 13 rebounds. The Knicks led 91-79 heading into the fourth quarter. OG Anunoby scored 14 points and had eight rebounds. Article continues below this ad Hawks stats to know CJ McCollum was brilliant with 32 points. The veteran guard was 12 of 22 from the field. After allowing at least 29 points in each of the first three quarters, the Hawks defense allowed 15 points in the fourth quarter. Young star Jalen Johnson struggled for much of the game, but finished with 17 points and eight rebounds. Off the bench, Jonathan Kuminga scored 19 points. Quin Snyder’s team only held the lead for 3% of the game. What’s next? Game 3 is Thursday in Atlanta.Article continues below this adMake the Times Union a Preferred Source on Google to see more of our journalism when you search.Add Preferred SourceThe Knicks and Hawks are tied 1-1 in their best-of-7 series.Josh Hart of the New York Knicks dunks against the Atlanta Hawks in the first quarter during Game 2 of the Eastern Conference first round NBA playoffs at Madison Square Garden on April 20, 2026 in New York City.Al Bello/Getty Images End 4th quarter: Hawks 107, Knicks 106 Hawks pull it off 10:47 p.m.: Atlanta outscores New York 28-15 in the fourth quarter to win Game 2.Article continues below this ad Jalen Brunson 3 brings NY closer 10:44 p.m.: The Hawks led 107-103 before a Brunson 3. Buckle up. Knicks lead it 100-99 late in 4th 10:34 p.m.: The Hawks are off to a 20-9 start to the fourth quarter.Article continues below this adNew York calls for timeout, with the ball, with 2:43 left. Knicks take 100-92 lead 10:28 p.m.: A bucket from Jalen Brunson leads to an Atlanta timeout.New York is up 100-92. Hawks are within striking distance after a 13-9 start to the period.Article continues below this ad Stars back into the game 10:22 p.m.: After a break, New York’s Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns, and Atlanta’s Jalen Johnson, check back in.It’s time to buckle up.Knicks lead 96-87 with 7:38 to go.Article continues below this ad Hawks ain't quitting 10:15 p.m.: A 4-0 start to the fourth quarter for Atlanta and Mike Brown takes a timeout.New York leads 91-83 with 10:30 left in regulation. Knicks trying to close it out 10:13 p.m.: The Knicks bring a lead into the fourth quarter and are 46-2 in that situation this season.Article continues below this adNew York leads 91-79 to start the period. End 3rd quarter: Knicks 91, Hawks 79 10:12 p.m.: After three quarters, some highlights. CJ McCollum had a game-high 26 points. Six Knicks have scored at least 10 points. Jalen Brunson had a team-high 19 points on 7 of 18 shooting. The Knicks outscored Atlanta 30-25 in the third period. Article continues below this ad Knicks in control heading to the 4th quarter 10:10 p.m.: The Knicks own a double-digit lead heading to the final period.Jalen Brunson has 19 points to lead New York, while Karl-Anthony Towns is up to 18. Knicks building lead, techs handed out 10:04 p.m.: A 3-pointer from big man Karl-Anthony Towns sends the MSG crowd into an uproar, and the Knicks are up 89-77 with 1:50 left in the third quarter.Article continues below this adShortly after the 3, CJ McCollum and Jose Alvarado each get a technical foul. Knicks leading late in 3rd quarter 9:58 p.m.: The Knicks own an 84-75 lead with 3:21 left in the third period.Jalen Brunson is up to 19 points for New York, which has also received 15 points from Josh Hart.Article continues below this adCJ McCollum has scored a game-high 24 points for the Hawks. Celebs in the house at MSG 9:53 p.m.: Hoping to see a Knicks win, there are plenty of famous faces in the crowd tonight at Madison Square Garden.Among the celebrities in attendance are actor Timothée Chalamet, gymnast Suni Lee, actor Ben Stiller rapper Fat Joe, Mets owner Steve Cohen and, of course, director Spike Lee.Article continues below this ad Balanced scoring leads Knicks 9:49 p.m.: Up 77-64 with 7:27 left in the third quarter, the Knicks have six players with at least 10 points.Josh Hart’s 15 points lead New York. Knicks stretch lead to double-digits 9:45 p.m.: After free throws from Jalen Brunson, the Knicks lead 75-64 with 7:58 left in the third quarter.Article continues below this adNew York is up 1-0 in this best-of-7 series. Knicks, Hawks back after halftime 9:39 p.m.: After the break, the teams are back on the floor at Madison Square Garden.The Hawks start the third quarter down 61-54.Article continues below this ad End 2nd quarter: Knicks 61, Hawks 54 9:23 p.m.: At the half, some highlights. CJ McCollum is leading all scorers with 18 points. He scored 11 points in the second quarter. Jalen Brunson has 12 points to lead New York. Mitchell Robinson has 11 points for the Knicks, while Mikal Bridges and Josh Hart each have 10 points. Jalen Brunson heating up 9:19 p.m.: The Knicks star is heating up.Article continues below this adJalen Brunson is up to 10 points late in the second quarter. Knicks, Hawks tied at 48 late in first half 9:13 p.m.: Game 2 is shaping up to be a good one.With the Knicks owning a 1-0 lead in the series, the teams are tied 48-48 with 2:58 left in the second quarter.Article continues below this adThe Hawks have outscored New York 25-16 in the second quarter. Knicks back on top 9:05 p.m.: After Atlanta briefly took a lead, New York has roared back.The Knicks are up 45-39 with 5:20 left in the second quarter.Article continues below this adNew York is shooting 50% from the field. Mitchell Robinson leading Knicks 9:02 p.m.: Backup center Mitchell Robinson has scored a game-high 10 points for the Knicks midway through the second quarter.Robinson has made 5 of 5 shots from the field.Article continues below this adNew York leads 40-36. Hawks coming back in New York 8:55 p.m.: Atlanta is off to an 11-3 start to the second quarter and has pulled within 35-34 with 8:37 left to halftime.CJ McCollum is up to a game-high nine points for Atlanta.Article continues below this ad Early Atlanta spark 8:51 p.m.: The Hawks have scored five of the second quarter’s first six points.New York leads 33-28 early in the period. End 1st quarter: Knicks lead Hawks 32-23 8:45 p.m.: Highlights from the opening periodArticle continues below this ad Mikal Bridges had eight points for the Knicks Off the bench, Mitchell Robinson scored six points for New York. Also adding six points was Josh Hart. For the Hawks, CJ McCollum scored seven points. Late in the quarter, Robinson and Atlanta’s Dyson Daniels were involved in a brief skirmish. Robinson walked atop Daniels after setting a pick on him, and the two had words after that. Robinson netted a technical foul for his role in the altercation. Officials review play, no flagrant called against Hawks 8:33 p.m.: After reviewing a play that saw Jalen Brunson elbowed in the head, a call against Dyson Daniels stays a common foul.The Knicks lead 20-13 with 4:09 left in the first quarter.Article continues below this ad Hawks' Mouhamed Gueye suffers apparent injury 8:24 p.m.: After missing a dunk, Atlanta’s Mouhamed Gueye is unable to get up.The game comes to a stop after a timeout to check on Gueye, who was able to exit the court on his own.The Knicks lead 17-9 with 5:33 left in the opening quarter.Article continues below this ad Knicks lead Hawks midway through 1st quarter 8:18 p.m.: After a Jalen Brunson 3, Atlanta's Quin Snyder calls for timeout.The Knicks are out to a 15-9 lead with 7:05 left in the first quarter.Josh Hart leads the Knicks with six points.Article continues below this ad Josh Hart adding early offense 8:15 p.m.: Not always a scorer for the Knicks, Josh Hart is off to a great start.He has four early points, including two from an emphatic jam, and the Knicks are out to a 10-4 lead. Knicks looking for hot start 8:09 p.m.: With a 1-0 series lead, the Knicks are trying to find their way to a 2-0 start in their best-of-7 series with the Hawks.Article continues below this adNew York is a -235 money-line favorite tonight, according to Fanduel.Actor Timothée Chalamet and actor Ben Stiller attend Game 2 of the Eastern Conference first round NBA playoffs at Madison Square Garden on April 20, 2026 in New York City.Al Bello/Getty Images Tonight’s starting lineups The Knicks lead the best-of-7 series 1-0 ahead of tonight’s 8 p.m. game. Here are tonight’s starting lineups.Article continues below this ad Knicks OG Anunoby Mikal Bridges Jalen Brunson Josh Hart Karl-Anthony Towns Hawks Nickeil Alexander-Walker Dyson Daniels Jalen Johnson CJ McCollum Onyeka Okongwu Article continues below this adThe officiating crew for tonight's game is Zach Zarba (crew chief), Karl Lane (referee), John Butler (umpire) and Mousa Dagher (alternate). Top scorers in NBA playoffs Through one game in every series, there have been 23 players to score at least 20 points.Article continues below this adIn the Knicks vs. Hawks series, four players have reached that mark. Cade Cunningham, Pistons, 39 Victor Wembanyama, Spurs, 35 Donovan Mitchell, Cavs, 32 Deni Avdija, Blazers, 30 Jamal Murray, Nuggets, 30 Jalen Brunson, Knicks, 28 Luke Kennard, Lakers, 27 Jaylen Brown, Celtics, 26 CJ McCollum, Hawks, 26 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Thunder, 25 Nikola Jokić, Nuggets, 25 Jayson Tatum, Celtics, 25 Karl-Anthony Towns, Knicks, 25 RJ Barrett, Raptors, 24 Max Strus, Cavs, 24 Paolo Banchero, Magic, 23 Devin Booker, Suns, 23 Jalen Johnson, Hawks, 23 Anthony Edwards, Timberwolves, 22 James Harden, Cavs, 22 Jalen Williams, Thunder, 22 Scottie Barnes, Raptors, 21 Tyrese Maxey, 76ers, 21 Hawks' injury update: Onyeka Okongwu Hawks starting center Onyeka Okongwu is listed as questionable for tonight’s 8 p.m. game against the Knicks. Okongwu, who scored 19 points and grabbed eight rebounds in Game 1, is dealing with right-knee inflammation and will be a game-time decision for head coach Quin Snyder.Article continues below this adThe Hawks are already thin in the frontcourt, with center Jock Landale out with an ankle injury and not expected to return until at least May 2. If Okongwu is unable to play, the Hawks will likely rely on backup center Mouhamed Gueye for more minutes. Gueye scored three points and grabbed three rebounds in 11 minutes in Game 1. Knicks vs. Hawks odds As of Monday late afternoon, the Knicks were -260 favorites tonight against the Hawks, according to Fanduel. The game’s over/under total is 217.5 and the Knicks are favored by 6.5 points. Knicks odds Moneyline: -260 To win the series: -450 To win the title: +2200 Article continues below this ad Hawks odds Moneyline: +215 To win the series: +350 To win the title: +22500 How to watch the New York Knicks vs. Atlanta Hawks Tonight’s 8 p.m. ET game between the New York Knicks and Atlanta Hawks is being broadcast on NBC and streamed on Peacock.Article continues below this ad Tale of two halves: Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns Knicks point guard Jalen Brunson (28 points, 7 assists) started Game 1 on a tear, hitting his first six shots and scoring 19 points in the first quarter and 22 in the first half. In the second half, Brunson used the pick-and-roll, and big man Karl-Anthony Towns took over, scoring 19 of his 25 points and energizing the Madison Square Garden crowd down the stretch.The Knicks' top two regular-season scorers, Brunson (25 ppg) and Towns (20.1 ppg), have improved their chemistry on and off the court since the duo became teammates in 2024.“I think we’ve grown as teammates, we’ve grown as friends, and it’s contributing to the way we’re playing,” Brunson said.Article continues below this ad Knicks' Mike Brown: Energy at MSG is 'different' Saturday’s 113-102 win over the Hawks was Mike Brown’s first career playoff victory as head coach of the Knicks. Brown, who served as an assistant coach under Steve Kerr during the Golden State Warriors' dynasty, is no stranger to playoff atmospheres. Still, he couldn’t help but notice the fans' energy at Madison Square Garden.“It always feels special walking into MSG; you know, I pinch myself every time I walk in,” he said. “You can feel the energy of the fans, you can feel the energy of the building, you can feel the energy from fans even outside, so it’s definitely different.” Knicks vs. Hawks: Playoff schedule The best-of-seven series continues tonight, with New York leading 1-0.Article continues below this ad Game 1: New York 113, Atlanta 102 Game 2: Monday at New York, 8 p.m., NBC Game 3: Thursday at Atlanta, 7 p.m., Prime Video Game 4: Saturday, April 25 at Atlanta, 6 p.m., NBC Game 5: Tuesday, April 28 at New York, TBA* Game 6: Thursday, April 30 at Atlanta, TBA* Game 7: Saturday, May 2 at New York, TBA* *if necessary Players to know for Knicks, Hawks New York Knicks Karl-Anthony Towns averaged 20.1 points and 11.9 rebounds for the Knicks in the regular season. Jalen Brunson is averaging 25.4 points and 8.5 assists over his past 10 games. Article continues below this adAtlanta Hawks Dyson Daniels scored 11.9 points per game and averaged 6.8 rebounds and 5.9 assists per game during the regular season for the Hawks. Nickeil Alexander-Walker is averaging 24.1 points, 3.6 rebounds and 3.6 assists over his past 10 games. Regular-season series at a glance The Knicks won the regular-season series against the Hawks 2-1.Article continues below this ad April 6: Knicks 108, Hawks 105 Jan. 2: Hawks 111, Knicks 99 Dec. 27: Knicks 128, Hawks 125 April 20, 2026|Updated April 20, 2026 11:05 p.m.Michael Kelly joined the Times Union in March 2024 and became the newspaper's executive sports editor later that year.
